instruction: Sort all sales representatives by their January sales in ascending order (lowest to highest).

metadata.explanation: Task requires sorting sales reps by January sales (column B) in ascending order. Verified with Python: January values sorted ascending are [220, 229, 231, 255, 429, 563, 696, 710, 752, 767]. Evaluator checks if column B contains these values in this order after sorting.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts column B (January sales) values from rows 2-11
Metric correctly compares values in sequential order (not just set equality), verifying ascending sort
Expected values [220, 229, 231, 255, 429, 563, 696, 710, 752, 767] are correctly sorted in ascending order
Postconfig appropriately saves file (Ctrl+S) before reading to ensure fresh state
Partial credit logic makes sense for sorting verification
Evaluator can distinguish between sorted state (values in expected order) and unsorted state (original order)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor edge case: Evaluator only checks column B values, not whether sales rep names (column A) are correctly reordered with their sales. This means someone could theoretically pass by manually typing sorted values into column B without actually sorting the rows. However, this is an unlikely scenario and the current approach is sufficient for verifying that proper spreadsheet sorting was performed.
Consider also checking column A (sales rep names) order to verify entire rows were sorted together, not just column B values replaced
